failures.criterion: A token is useless once its life has passed, and introspection answers only a live access token: 'a token ... one that has expired [is] answered as simply not live' (packages/envoy/internal/broker/oauth/introspect.go:52-55), 'Introspection is what the broker knows about one of its access tokens' (:13).
failures.evidence: Introspection answers a machine login's refresh token `active: true`, with the access token's expiry as `exp`, and keeps answering it live after that expiry has passed. Live binary (my throwaway probe, BROKER_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECONDS=2, a device-grant machine login approved through POST /v1/credential-requests/{id}/approve by the listed API account): 2.5 s after the login, POST /v1/oauth/introspect of the refresh token -> `200 {"active":true,"scope":"machine","exp":1792919259,"client_id":"agent-secrets-helper","jkt":"5TWK-..."}` at now=1792919259, while the same login's access token -> `200 {"active":false}`. In-process with a one-second access life: `{Active:true ... Scope:machine ExpiresAt:1792919196 ClientID:agent-secrets-helper ...}` at now=1792919197. The answer carries no token type, so a resource server cannot tell the two apart. Introspect passes oauth2.AccessToken as a hint, and the library falls through to the refresh-token store when the access lookup misses; the first return value, which names which kind it found, is discarded (introspect.go:57). Red test (commit 5e70626e8906): `cd packages/envoy && BROKER_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<url> go test -count=1 -run TestIntrospectionAnswersOnlyAnAccessToken ./internal/broker/oauth/` -> FAIL on both subtests, 'Introspect of a refresh token = {Active:true ...}, want not live and nothing else'.

failures.criterion: The pull request's Change bullets are true (skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: the implementer keeps them true).
failures.evidence: The bullet 'A pod's token is accepted only while it is bound to a live pod' is not what the code does, and the same claim is in exchange.Set.Pod's comment ('a bound one proves a pod of this cluster is running right now', packages/envoy/internal/broker/exchange/exchange.go:226-227). The exchange verifies a pod token offline against the issuer's published keys and only requires the `kubernetes.io.pod.uid` claim to be present; it never asks the cluster whether that pod exists. A token whose pod has been deleted is exchanged until its own `exp`, which the exchange allows up to 24 hours ahead (kubernetesTolerance, exchange.go:87). Observed: the implementer's live run and mine exchange tokens bound to `pod-uid-1`, `pod-claims-iat-23h-ago` and others on a broker that has no cluster at all, each answered 200; a token with `iat` 23 hours ago was answered 200. The spec accepted this trade ('trades immediate revocation of that token for needing no access to the cluster's own interface'); the bullet and the comment need to say 'bound to a pod' and name how long a deleted pod's token stays exchangeable, so the person merging reads the risk the code carries.
